title: X-NavDP Generalizes Navigation Diffusion Policies Across Embodiments
summary: Navigation diffusion policies are normally pretrained on demonstrations from a fully-informed oracle planner tuned to one nominal robot, which limits them to that body and to easy scenarios. X-NavDP post-trains such policies with reinforcement learning using group Q-score reweighted matching, addressing the unstable policy gradients that come from a diffusion policy's intractable likelihood. The result is reactive behaviour — escaping dead ends, detouring long obstacles — from onboard local observations across different embodiments.
whyItMatters: Earlier attempts to RL-finetune diffusion policies produced only marginal gains because the likelihood term is intractable. Reweighting by group Q-scores sidesteps that and makes post-training actually move the policy, which is the missing step between a demonstration-cloned navigator and one that improvises when the oracle's assumptions break.
